new_statements.rule_in_words: No stress rule is stated. Caron, who did fieldwork on Dììr (Dir) and Nyámzax (Langas = Nyamzak), describes them, with the rest of the Polci cluster other than Polci proper, as two-tone languages (Low vs High); Caron 2006 repeats that all his SBW languages except Zaar and Gùùs, including Langas and Dir, have two tone levels. No opened source says anything about word stress, accent or prominence in Dir, Nyamzak or Mbarimi.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Caron only notes that the 3-tone (Polci, Zaar) vs 2-tone (rest of cluster) split makes tone-marking of reconstructed Common Polci forms difficult.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the lexical/grammatical tone system (number of tone levels) of the cluster languages; it comes from a 7-page comparative-morphology paper, not a phonological description, so its silence on stress is weak evidence about stress. Later Caron papers show grammatical tone (floating High/Low marking number on the verb in Dir and Langas).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog lund1276 (name 'Lundur', dialect lang1332 Langas) = ISO 639-3 nzr Nyamzak-Dir-Mbarimi, created 2023 by splitting plj Polci (ISO CR 2022-023); Glottolog classifies it under Polci > Zuli. Three varieties: Nyamzak (= Langas, Nyamzax, Laŋas; villages Langas and Lundur, Miri District, Bauchi LGA; c. 900), Dir (= Diir, Dììr; c. 500) and Mbarimi (= Baram, Barang, Mbaram; Baram Dutse village; c. 1000). Caron's 2005 statement names 'Dììr' and 'Nyámzax (Langas)' explicitly as fieldwork languages and 'Barang' and 'Lundur' among the cluster members, so 'the others are two-tone languages' covers Dir and Nyamzak first-hand and Mbarimi (Barang) by listing only. Name trap: Caron 2009 and Blench equate 'Mbarmi/Barma' with Zul (zlu, zulq1240), a different language, whereas Mbarimi = Baram/Mbaram (this languoid). Nothing describes Mbarimi specifically.
